explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/830: a, b form an amicable pair if σ(a) = σ(b) = a + b; are there infinitely many amicable pairs? IsAmicable a b requires σ₁(a) = a + b, σ₁(b) = a + b and a ≠ b; the distinctness is the standard convention (otherwise perfect numbers would count as pairs, changing the question), and the statement {(a,b) | IsAmicable a b}.Infinite is the 'yes' answer. Faithful.
